_metadata.description: Reviewed GHOST-SUSPECT findings from verify_backed_studies_citations.py --strict. A suspect blocks the release gate until it is reviewed here with a rationale that states why the live PubMed record does support the entry. Removing an entry re-arms the gate for that citation.

reviewed.live_title: An Extract of Glycyrrhiza glabra (GutGard) Alleviates Symptoms of Functional Dyspepsia
reviewed.rationale: False positive of the word-overlap heuristic, not a wrong-topic citation. The entry is Deglycyrrhizinated Licorice and its own notes cite this PMID for exactly this claim: 'The strongest modern trials are on the standardized GutGard extract for functional dyspepsia'. Glycyrrhiza glabra is licorice; the heuristic compares the live title against the stored ingredient words 'deglycyrrhizinated' and 'glycyrrhizin', which the botanical binomial does not string-match. Topic, extract name and indication all agree.

reviewed.live_title: Bioavailable turmeric extract for knee osteoarthritis: a randomized, non-inferiority trial versus paracetamol
reviewed.rationale: False positive of the title-only word-overlap heuristic. The live PubMed abstract's Methods section explicitly identifies the tested intervention as BCM-95 500 mg twice daily. This entry is scoped to the BCM-95/CurcuGreen formulation and explicitly disclaims evidence for the finished Life Extension retail product, so the PMID supports the authored formulation-level claim.

Primary PubMed identifies this as the retraction of lutein/zeaxanthin adolescent-myopia review PMID41573009 (DOI10.18240/ijo.2026.02.21). The corrected entry cites the notice only to exclude that original from affirmative evidence. Remaining PMID28661438 concerns a macular-carotenoid combination in 48 young adults, not isolated lutein or adolescent myopia prevention. A generic notice title is a title-heuristic miss; no affirmative credit or whole-record clearance is granted.
